title: SwarmKit Workspace
description: Deployment-level config: identity, governance, model providers, MCP registry, storage. See design §9.3 and design/details/workspace-schema-v1.md.

command_packs.description: Local command packs — the sibling of `mcp_servers` for capabilities that already exist as binaries and would otherwise need a wrapper server written for them.

channels.description: Named channels a swarm can reach a human on, exposed to agents as the `channels` skills. Without this block the notification transports exist but nothing can address them.

annotations.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata the runtime ignores. For enterprise use: cost_center, team, environment, compliance tags, etc.

policy_language.description: §21 open question — default yaml for v1.0.

limits.description: Circuit breaker thresholds. Prevents runaway execution and cost overruns.

max_steps_per_agent.description: Maximum execution steps per individual agent before abort.

max_steps_per_run.description: Maximum total steps across all agents in a single run. Default: 500.

max_cost_per_run_usd.description: Maximum estimated LLM cost (USD) per run before abort.

decision_skills.description: Mandatory decision skills that fire at specified trigger points. Topologies inherit these and can override by id.

credential_ref.$comment: Credentials are never stored literally in workspace.yaml. Each entry is a reference with a uniform shape: { source, config }. The runtime dispatches to the SecretsProvider identified by `source` and validates `config` against that provider's contract. See design note for the provider list and per-source config shapes. `source: plugin` additionally requires `provider_id` to identify a SecretsProvider registered via entry points.

source.description: Which SecretsProvider resolves this credential. `oauth` resolves through the runtime's token store: the value is obtained by logging in once from the portal or CLI, and refreshed automatically at the point of use — see design/details/mcp-oauth.md and credential-service.md.

provider_id.description: Required when source=plugin. Names the registered SecretsProvider.

config.description: Provider-specific configuration. Runtime validates shape per source.

allOf.$comment: An oauth credential names the server it was obtained for. The token itself is never here: it lives encrypted in the runtime's own store, keyed by (credential, owner).

env.description: Environment variables passed to a stdio server. Values support ${VAR} expansion from the runtime process environment, and {credential.<ref>} which resolves through the workspace `credentials` block (the same substitution command packs use). Prefer {credential.…} over ${VAR} for secrets: it keeps the secret out of the runtime's own environment, so it cannot leak into an unrelated subprocess.

cwd.description: Working directory for stdio servers. Supports ${VAR} expansion. Defaults to workspace root.

credentials_ref.description: A key_ref resolved through the workspace `credentials` block — 'credentials:<name>', 'env:VAR' or 'file:/path'. For transport=http the resolved secret is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`, which is what OAuth-protected remote MCP servers expect. For stdio it is available to `env` values as {credential.<this-ref>}. Until 1.204.0 this field was parsed and read by nothing, while `env`'s own description told authors to use it for secrets — so a server configured exactly as documented connected with no credentials at all.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for transport=http. Values support ${VAR} and {credential.<ref>}. For a server whose scheme is not bearer — an API key in a custom header, say — set it here instead of `credentials_ref`. An explicit Authorization header wins over the one derived from `credentials_ref`.

sandbox_image.description: Docker image for sandboxed servers. Defaults to swarmkit-mcp-sandbox (Python + mcp SDK). Use node:22-slim for Node.js servers.

permission.description: Governance permission tier for this server's tools. open: skip governance checks. cautious (default): reads auto-approved, writes go through governance. strict: all calls require explicit approval. readonly: write operations denied.

permission_overrides.description: Per-tool permission overrides. Keys are MCP tool names, values are permission tiers that override the server default.

effects.description: Whether each tool reads or writes, keyed by MCP tool name. Consulted by `permission: readonly`, which allows a tool only when it is known to read. Declared here wins over the server's own `readOnlyHint` annotation, because this is the half the operator controls; a tool with neither is `unknown` and is denied under readonly rather than guessed at. Until 1.199.0 write-ness was inferred by substring-scanning the tool name, which denied `get_dataset` and `read_asset` on 'set' and let `truncate_table` and `purge_cache` through.

checkpoints.description: LangGraph run-state checkpointer. The one block that does NOT inherit storage.runtime: postgres here needs `pip install 'swarmkit-runtime[postgres]'`, so it is opt-in rather than implied.

backend.description: Checkpointer backend. Defaults to sqlite at .swarmkit/state/checkpoints.db.

url.description: Connection URL for the postgres backend. Supports ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default} interpolation. Optional: inherits storage.runtime.url when omitted.

audit.description: Append-only audit trail. Inherits storage.runtime unless it overrides it.

backend.description: Audit backend. Defaults to whatever storage.runtime resolves to. ('agt' was accepted here until 1.130.0, but no writer ever implemented it — selecting it silently wrote sqlite.)

url.description: Connection URL for the postgres backend. Supports ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default} interpolation. Optional: inherits storage.runtime.url when omitted.

artifacts.description: Where pipeline stage outputs live. Defaults to `database` on the storage.runtime engine. Read by the runtime since the bundled orchestrator shipped, but undeclarable until 1.130.0 — `additionalProperties: false` rejected the very key the code looked for.

path.description: filesystem backend: root directory. Defaults to .swarmkit/artifacts.

bucket.description: s3 backend: bucket name (requires the boto3 optional dep).

database_url.description: database backend: override the inherited connection URL.

runtime.description: Backend for jobs, conversations, usage, pipeline sagas, artifacts, fleet enrollment and governed memory. Every other storage block inherits this one unless it overrides it. Defaults to sqlite at .swarmkit/store.sqlite.

backend.description: Storage backend. sqlite (default, zero config) or postgres (production, shared).

url.description: Connection URL for the postgres backend. Supports ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default} interpolation. May also be supplied as SWARMKIT_STORE_URL or DATABASE_URL, which take precedence over this file.

context_compression.description: Opt-in read-side compression of bulk tool/MCP output before it re-enters an agent's context. Off by default. Never applied to the audit log or the inter-agent contract. Env vars SWARMKIT_CONTEXT_COMPRESSION and SWARMKIT_CONTEXT_COMPRESSION_MIN_BYTES override the default per deployment. See design/details/context-compression.md.

overrides.description: Per-surface rules matched by tool-name and/or server-id glob. The first override that matches wins; otherwise the top-level backend/min_bytes apply.

compression_backend.description: Compression backend. off (default): no compression. columnar: built-in lossless JSON minify + array-of-uniform-dicts rewrite to {columns, rows}. headtail: reversible-lossy — keep head+tail, elide the middle, recallable via the context_retrieve tool (for lossy-tolerant surfaces like logs). plugin: a custom ContextCompressor named by backend_class.

compression_backend_class.description: Fully-qualified Python class path of a custom ContextCompressor (used when backend=plugin), e.g. 'my_pkg.compressors.LearnedCompressor'.

compression_min_bytes.description: Payloads smaller than this (in characters) are left untouched — avoids overhead on small results.

compression_override.description: A per-surface compression rule. At least one of match / match_server is required.

match.description: Glob matched against the tool/skill name (e.g. 'get-logs', 'frigate*').

match_server.description: Glob matched against the MCP server id backing the tool (e.g. 'frigate', 'logs-*').

planning.description: Default planning behavior for all topologies in this workspace. Topology-level planning overrides these defaults.

scope_required.description: Leaders must call create-scope before synthesis.

two_phase.description: Enforce two-phase planning for all topologies.

synthesis_roles.description: Default synthesis/output roles for all topologies: auto-wired to depend on research tasks so they run last. Defaults to ['self', 'document-writer']. Topology-level planning overrides this.

synthesizer_role.description: Default role name for the automatic synthesis step. Defaults to 'synthesizer'. Topology-level planning overrides this.

synthesis.description: Automatic synthesis config. When set, the compiler invokes a large-context model directly with all research results instead of having the architect write the document.

provider.description: Model provider ID (e.g. google, openrouter, anthropic).

prompt.description: Custom system prompt for the synthesizer. Overrides the platform default. Use this to control document style, diagram generation (mermaid), grounding rules, and section handling.

decision_skill_binding.description: Binds a decision skill to a trigger point. Workspace bindings are inherited by all topologies; topology bindings can override by id.

id.description: Decision skill ID. Must exist in workspace skill registry.

trigger.description: When the skill fires: pre_input (before agent runs, validates user input), post_output (after agent output), checkpoint (between task batches), pre_synthesis (before final synthesis).

scope.description: Comma-separated agent IDs this binding applies to. Default '*' = all agents in the topology.

required.description: Whether a failing verdict from this skill STOPS the run. true (the default) means a `fail` rejects the output; false means the skill still runs and its rejection is advisory — logged, not fatal. It does NOT disable the binding: use `enabled: false` for that. Until 1.169.0 a falsey `required` silently discarded the binding, so an advisory skill was never evaluated at all.

config.description: Skill-specific configuration (confidence thresholds, retry limits, etc).

enabled.description: Whether this binding is active. Set false in a topology to switch off a binding inherited from the workspace. Separate from `required` because the two are different questions — whether a skill runs, and whether its verdict can stop the run.

server_config.description: Configuration for swarmkit serve mode. Controls job concurrency, timeouts, MCP server lifecycle, and canary deployments.

max_concurrent.description: Maximum number of concurrent topology executions.

enabled.description: Whether to start MCP servers at boot in serve mode.

canary.description: Canary deployment configuration. Routes traffic between topology versions by weight with optional auto-promotion. See design/details/canary-deployments.md.

routes.description: Canary routes. Each route splits traffic for one topology across multiple versions.

server_auth.description: HTTP authentication for swarmkit serve. Off by default (provider: none). For a non-loopback bind, leaving provider=none refuses to start unless require_on_nonloopback is false (default-secure). See design/details/control-plane/12-auth.md.

provider.description: none: open access (default; only safe on loopback). api_key: bearer tokens from a static key registry. jwt: OIDC-compliant JWT bearer tokens (RS256/ES256 + JWKS).

require_on_nonloopback.description: When true (default), a non-loopback bind (--host other than 127.0.0.1/::1) with provider=none refuses to start. Set false to allow an open non-loopback bind (not recommended).

server_auth_config.description: Provider-specific auth config. keys[] for api_key; issuer/audience/jwks_url/scopes_claim/client_id/scope for jwt; identity/identity_name for none.

audience.description: Expected token audience (provider: jwt). Default: swarmkit.

scopes_claim.description: JWT claim holding scopes (provider: jwt). Default: scope.

client_id.description: The browser's OIDC client registration (provider: jwt), advertised to clients via /auth-info. The server never uses it to validate anything — it advertises it because the portal ships as a pre-built static export, so a build-time env var would be fixed at publish and the same wheel serves every deployment. Without it the portal cannot start a sign-in flow.

scope.description: OIDC scopes the portal requests (provider: jwt), advertised via /auth-info. Default: openid profile email.

identity.description: Who the caller is asserted to be (provider: none). Default: anonymous. This mode already grants wildcard scopes and authorizes everything, so naming the operator confers no new capability — but the approval engine matches this value against members: in swarm/roles.yaml, so it is what makes a local gate approvable without standing up an identity provider. Asserted, not authenticated: the audit records provider=none.

identity_name.description: Display name for that identity (provider: none). Defaults to the identity itself.

server_auth_key.description: One API key. Grant scopes via a tier (read/run/admin → serve:* scopes) OR explicit scopes — not both.

key_ref.description: Reference to the secret, never a literal: 'env:VAR' or a credentials entry. Resolved at startup.

client_id.description: Stable id for this caller (appears in audit).

tier.description: Transport scope tier: read (observe) | run (+ execute) | admin (+ mutate artifacts/rollout). Expands to serve:* scopes.

scopes.description: Explicit scopes, as an alternative to tier (e.g. ['serve:read','serve:run']).

canary_route.description: Traffic splitting rule for a single topology.

topology.description: Topology name (matches metadata.name). Must exist in the workspace.

versions.description: Version entries. Weights must sum to 100.

canary_version.description: A single version in a canary route with its traffic weight and optional promotion criteria.

version.description: Topology version (semver). Must match a topology file's metadata.version.

weight.description: Percentage of traffic routed to this version (0-100).

promote_when.description: Auto-promotion criteria. When all conditions are met, this version is promoted to 100% traffic.

promote_criteria.description: Conditions that must ALL be met for auto-promotion of a canary version.

min_runs.description: Minimum number of completed runs before promotion is eligible.

error_rate_below.description: Maximum error rate (failed/total). E.g. 0.05 = 5% error rate threshold.

drift_below.description: Maximum average drift score. E.g. 0.30 = low drift tolerance.

window_minutes.description: Evaluation window in minutes. Only runs within this window count toward promotion criteria.

command_spec.description: A single command in a pack. `argv` is executed directly — there is no shell, so a substituted value can never become an argument or an operator.

argv.description: argv, executed with no shell. `{name}` placeholders are filled from the skill's declared inputs and are always passed as exactly one argument, never re-parsed. `{credential.*}` is rejected here — secrets reach a command through the pack's `env` only, so they cannot be model-placed, cannot appear in an audit line, and cannot be read from `ps`.

effects.description: Whether this command changes anything. Not inferrable from the binary — `curl` POSTs and `jq` takes `-i` — so the pack author declares it. Undeclared means `write`, so an unclassified command fails closed. `permission: readonly` denies every `write` command.

binary_requirement.description: A binary this pack needs, checked at workspace load rather than at run time. A topology that only runs where a binary happens to exist is less portable data than one that does not, and the failure should name the binary rather than surface as an exec error mid-run.

version.description: Constraint such as '>=1.7', compared against the binary's --version output. An unparseable version is a load error, not a silent pass.

command_pack.description: A named set of local commands exposed to skills through `implementation.type: command`. Governed exactly as an mcp_server is — the pack carries the permission tier, the skill carries `iam.required_scopes`.

permission.description: Governance permission tier for this pack's commands, matching mcp_server. open: skip governance checks. cautious (default): reads auto-approved, writes go through governance. strict: all calls require explicit approval. readonly: every command declaring `effects: write` is denied.

permission_overrides.description: Per-command tier overrides. Keys are command ids.

timeout_seconds.description: Pack default. A command with no ceiling can take a run down with it, so an omitted value means the built-in default, never unbounded.

timeout_overrides.description: Per-command timeout overrides in seconds. Keys are command ids.

max_output_bytes.description: Combined stdout+stderr ceiling. Exceeding it fails the call rather than truncating, since a truncated result read as complete is the worse outcome.

cwd.description: Working directory. Supports ${VAR} expansion. Defaults to workspace root.

env.description: Environment for every command in the pack. Supports ${VAR} expansion and `{credential.<ref>}` resolved against `credentials_ref`. This is the only place a secret may reach a command.

channel.$comment: A named destination a swarm can reach a human on. Named rather than global so a topology can route an infrastructure question to ops and a release question to engineering without a second workspace. The transports are the notification providers; this block is what makes them reachable. Tokens are never literal: `credentials_ref` names an entry in `credentials`. See design/details/channel-skills.md.

provider.description: Which transport carries this channel. Only `telegram` supports inbound replies (Bot API getUpdates); the others are send-only and `channel_replies` reports `unsupported` on them rather than returning an empty list.

credentials_ref.description: Names an entry in the workspace `credentials` block that resolves to the bot token or webhook URL. A literal token here would be a secret in a file people commit.

config.description: Provider-specific destination — e.g. `chat_id` for telegram, `channel` for slack. Validated by the runtime per provider.

inbound.description: Poll this channel for replies. Telegram only. `getUpdates` is single-consumer — two pollers on one token steal each other's updates and the loser silently sees nothing — so the runtime refuses a second poller for a token already being polled.

then.$comment: Inbound on discord/slack would need a held-open gateway socket or Socket Mode. Refused at validation rather than accepted and silently ignored.
